Text, Contrast & Readability: The 4.5 Rule

6 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

White text on a red background fails the web's own readability standard for normal-size text. So does white on bright orange, and white on yellow fails badly. Most Kenyan flyers you'll see this week make at least one of these mistakes.

Readability on a phone has a number attached to it. The W3C's accessibility guidelines (WCAG) say normal text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background; large text (about 24px, or about 18.5px bold) needs at least 3:1. These are minimums, not targets.

4.5 : 1
Minimum contrast for normal text under WCAG 2 Level AA; large text needs 3:1 (W3C)

How common colour combinations score on the WCAG formula

Text on backgroundContrast ratioVerdict
White on yellow (#FFD600)1.4 : 1Fails everything. Unreadable in sunlight
Light grey on white2.3 : 1Fails. The 'elegant' look that nobody can read
White on mid green (#4CAF50)2.8 : 1Fails, even for big headlines
White on bright orange (#FF6F00)2.8 : 1Fails, even for big headlines
White on red (#E53935)4.2 : 1OK for big headlines only, not small text
White on dark green (#1B5E20)7.9 : 1Passes comfortably
Black on yellow (#FFD600)14.9 : 1Excellent. Why road signs use it

Canva's hidden checker

Canva has a built-in accessibility check that most people never open: File → Accessibility → Check design accessibility. It flags text that is too small, colour combinations with poor contrast, and images missing alt text. Run it before you export anything important.

Three fixes for text on a busy photo

  • Text background: select the text, open Effects, choose Background. Canva drops a solid block behind the words, and you can lower its transparency to keep the photo visible.
  • Dark overlay: put a black rectangle over the whole photo and set transparency to around 30–50%. White text on top suddenly becomes readable.
  • Move the text to the plainest part of the photo (sky, wall, table top) instead of over faces or patterned fabric.
💡 What most creators miss

Your design will be seen on a cracked phone, at low brightness to save battery, in Nairobi sunshine, often half covered by app buttons. On TikTok, Reels and WhatsApp Status, the bottom and right edges are covered by captions, usernames and buttons. Keep key text in the centre-top area, and judge your design on your phone at half brightness, not on a laptop.

📋 One-message post structure
HEADLINE (6 words max): [e.g. Braids from KES 2,500 this week]
DETAIL (one line): [e.g. Kilimani, Tue–Sat, book by WhatsApp]
ACTION (one instruction): [e.g. DM 'BRAIDS' to book]

If you need more than this, make it a carousel, not a crowded single post.
✅ Do this today (under 15 minutes)
⚡ Quick check

Which of these passes the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast minimum for normal-size text?

Black on yellow scores about 14.9:1. White on red is about 4.2:1, so it falls just short for small text, and white on orange or mid green is only about 2.8:1. Bright, 'loud' colours often have poor contrast with white.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Readability has a number: aim for at least 4.5:1 contrast for normal text.
  2. Bright backgrounds (yellow, orange, mid green) with white text usually fail.
  3. Canva's File → Accessibility check flags small text and poor contrast for you.
  4. Keep key text away from the bottom and right edges on vertical formats.
